comment: The local-capacity principle, because it focuses on design choises, is too narrow for platforms that become national infrastructure. DHIS2 sustainability depends not only on documented technology but on a distributed HISP ecosystem: permanent ministry teams, local HISP groups, universities, academies, implementers, help desks, peer networks and country-to-country learning. These relationships retain knowledge, support upgrades and turn local requirements into reusable platform improvements.

public.text: The local-capacity principle, because it focuses on design choises, is too narrow for platforms that become national infrastructure. DHIS2 sustainability depends not only on documented technology but on a distributed HISP ecosystem: permanent ministry teams, local HISP groups, universities, academies, implementers, help desks, peer networks and country-to-country learning. These relationships retain knowledge, support upgrades and turn local requirements into reusable platform improvements.
public.suggestedRevision: Require a costed national capacity and support architecture: designated public-sector ownership; national and subnational core teams; local implementation/support organisations (HISP model as an example); university partnerships; academies, apprenticeship and mentoring; communities of practice; help-desk and escalation arrangements; succession; and recurrent budgets. Evaluate capacity as  infrastructure, to be developed and maintained over time--not as a one-off training deliverable.
